title: Squared (²) & Cubed (³) Symbols: Copy & Paste Exponents
meta_description: Copy and paste the squared (²) and cubed (³) symbols used for exponents and unit abbreviations like m² and cm³, plus why they work almost everywhere. Click to copy.
hero_tagline: The two superscript digits that predate the rest of the superscript set — for exponents, unit abbreviations, and "x squared" notation. Click any symbol to copy it instantly.
intro: ² and ³ (superscript two and three, U+00B2 and U+00B3) are the exponent characters behind x², E=mc², and unit abbreviations like m² and cm³. Unlike the rest of the superscript digits, they've been part of the standard Latin-1 character set since the 1980s — which is why they render correctly in far more places than ⁰, ¹, or ⁴–⁹.
